newsitem.title: USA: Maine storm causes power outages. [CORRECTED 23:57 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Maine storm causes power outages. [CORRECTED 23:57 GMT]

text.p: An estimated 40,000 customers of Central Maine Power were without electricity Tuesday (corrects from Thursday) because of a storm that dumped ice and heavy snow on the state, company officials said.
Trees and branches that have fallen across power lines had knocked out power to nearly 8.0 percent of CMP's customer base by Thursday afternoon, spokesman Mark Ishkanian said.
"Just as soon as we restore power to one customer it seems like we lose power to two more," said Ishkanian, adding; "the weather is not helping things."

The National Weather Service issued winter storm warnings for western and central interior sections of Maine. Ishkanian said CMP has brought in extra repair crews from New Hampshire, but weather conditions would determine when all service was restored.
